author: evergreen reporter
title: Woodbury man receives 30-year sentence for online sextortion targeting minors
text:
Timothy Lennard Gebhart, a 38-year-old resident of Woodbury, Minnesota, has been sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for crimes related to a long-running sextortion scheme targeting minors. U.S. District Judge Jerry W. Blackwell handed down the sentence, which also includes 10 years of supervised release following imprisonment.
According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Gebhart’s offenses included production and attempted production of child pornography, distribution of child pornography, and interstate communications with intent to extort. U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced the sentencing.
Authorities said that from July 2021 through September 2023, Gebhart used social media platforms such as Instagram and Snapchat to target children as young as twelve years old. He created at least 66 different Snapchat aliases and posed as a teenager or someone younger than his actual age in order to befriend victims.
Once he established contact with his victims, Gebhart convinced them to send sexually explicit photos and videos. He also sought sexual encounters with some of the minors.
After obtaining these materials, Gebhart threatened to share them with the victims’ classmates, friends, and family unless they provided additional explicit content. He further intimidated his victims by sending them disturbing videos depicting violent deaths and used hateful language in his threats.
In delivering the sentence, Judge Blackwell described Gebhart’s actions as a “deliberate, persistent sextortion scheme.”
The investigation was conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Woodbury Police Department, and Indiana State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney David M. Classen prosecuted the case.
